title: Communication Skills
notes: A message moves from a sender to a receiver through a channel. Noise is anything that distorts it: a poor line, jargon, or a listener who is distracted. Feedback is the receiver's reply, and it shows whether the message arrived.

Before speaking or writing, name the purpose — to inform, request, persuade, or apologise — and the audience. A request to a teacher needs a polite opener and a clear ask. The same request to a classmate can be shorter.
Active listening means attending, then restating the other person's point in your own words before you answer. Preparing your reply while they are still speaking loses their actual claim.
Speech uses tone, pause, and gesture. Writing must put those cues into word choice and punctuation. An email still needs a subject line, a greeting, the request in the first lines, and a closing.

A barrier can be linguistic (unfamiliar words), cultural (a gesture that means something else), or psychological (fear of looking wrong). Name the barrier, then choose a simpler word or a question that checks understanding.
